List of wendover crap productions  1. “How Tesla Fumbled” (February 2023)

This is by far the biggest flashpoint. Multiple detailed critiques (including other YouTubers and Reddit analyses) called it a one-sided hit piece filled with problems, such as:
Heavy reliance on outdated data (e.g., 2018 delivery “hell” when Tesla was producing a fraction of its later volume).
Misleading or incomplete product comparisons (e.g., mixing Mach-E specs that didn’t correspond to an actual real-world configuration).
Claims about competitors (Ford, GM, Rivian, Lucid, BYD) that understated Tesla’s volume, profitability, or delivery advantages at the time.
Emphasis on Consumer Reports reliability rankings while downplaying Tesla’s strong results on owner satisfaction surveys.
Framing of service centers, brand loyalty, and other issues that critics said lacked current context.

replies.text:
"If both cost the same"
That misses the point. If both cost the same and have the same safety, then it will only be whichever gets you were you want to go faster or random fanboy/hatred decisions.

But if one on paper is considered safer while being 3x more expensive than the other, then which do you pick? That's the real question here. And to add to it, the cheaper one is starting to ramp up extremely quickly while the other is already in your area and has been for some time. So the one is considered safer on paper, but the other is far cheaper, able to get to you faster by having more, and is still extremely safe in real world conditions. But the expensive one is also on the app you already have installed and set up on your phone with all of your payment info. And its still cheaper than what you got before while getting you where you want to go in a reasonable time. 

So with all of that said, which do you get? Personally, I will use which ever I can at first. However, I will prefer Tesla's as I know so much more about the vehicles, safety, and entertainment setup. It will work far better for me. Eventually, the costs will likely win out as well. However, that will be a while and it might not ever be enough to matter.

replies.author: @anthonypelchat
replies.text:
I agree that no company needs to offer level 3. Level 4 though is basically Level 5 with borders. No big deal. Further, Level 5's vague definition is pretty pointless. Are you not Level 5 if you can drive everywhere in the US but Canada or Mexico? Or are you not Level 5 because you can't drive during a tornado, hurricane, flooding, or other massive natural disasters that keep humans from driving as well? Or maybe you aren't Level 5 because you don't drive offroad or handle other niche situations.

Level 4 covers all basic driving needs and never needs a dedicated driver.
